topComments.author: SpeakingOfBrad
topComments.text: I had the idea for BIGWORDS.PAGE when I wanted to display a message on a tablet that I had remote management control over, but no physical access. Configuring it to be a kiosk browser is easy, but how do I get the browser to show my message? So I made the URL be the message. It uses a URL fragment to configure the message. Browsers don't send URL fragments to the server, so I never see your message. There's no backend, and no storage. All parameters are documented, so generating a message link is easy. There's also a built-in editor to make it extra easy. https://bigwords.page/#Hello,%20HN!&bg=ff6600&fg=000000&font... There are a few extra features like slides, animations, and countdowns and timers. QR codes too. Not too fancy, but hopefully enough to be useful. I know the uses for this are pretty niche. But it may be one of those things that you keep as a nugget in your brain, a tool in your back pocket. Not something you use often, but when you do it makes things just a little bit easier. topComments.text: Author here. I bought this CD in 2011 and spent 15 years failing to find out who made it. The band charted at #47 on the UK Independent Singles Chart in June 2006, so it was a real, professionally made, commercially distributed record, and I couldn't find anything online: no credits, no fingerprint match, no company registration for the label, nothing on streaming. Part of the answer turned out to be that their website was Flash, so it was never meaningfully indexed, and their MySpace was never mirrored. A band can be entirely findable in 2006 and entirely gone by 2026 depending on which technologies they happened to pick. stories.author: ibobev

topComments.author: weinzierl
topComments.text: The "integer arithmetic paradigm" would mean either checking after (almost) every operation or living with potentially incorrect results. The first is terribly inefficient, the second is just wrong (even if insanely common). This is sad because there is no reason at all why integers couldn’t follow what OP calls the "float paradigm" . It doesn’t even have to be slow. Most modern processors (if we ignore x86) support some form of sticky arithmetic flags. Unfortunately, programming languages don’t support them, so they aren’t used. There is also something to be said about the special treatment division by zero gets.

jobs.text: I’m Chris, VP Engineering at Fazeshift. We’re nine engineers plus our Founder/CTO and me, and I’m hiring someone who can help us do more, better: increase both what we can build and the quality and sophistication of the software we build. Accounts receivable sounds boring until you look under the hood. Our customers already run on ERPs, CRMs, banks, billing systems, payment processors, spreadsheets, and internal software, so we have to understand state across systems we don’t control, act safely in them, and recover when reality disagrees with what an API says should have happened. A timeout doesn’t necessarily mean a write failed. Webhooks can arrive late or twice. A payment may not contain enough information to identify an invoice. You’ll own meaningful problems from ambiguity through design, implementation, rollout, and production, and you’ll work directly with the people affected by what you build. quantaArticles.description: Scientists assumed that energy flows in only one direction in a turbulent system. What they didn’t know, until they looked closely at brine shrimp, was that a simple factor can reverse the flow.
quantaArticles.author: Stephen Ornes

quantaArticles.title: What Does the Fourth Dimension Actually Look Like?

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Multi-Agent Patterns from Spotify’s AI Powered Advertising Platform
infoqArticles.description: Pratik Rasam discusses how Spotify Ads Manager runs production-grade multi-agent systems at scale using Google ADK Java. He shares key architectural patterns, domain ownership models, deterministic guardrails, and tracing-based evaluation strategies, detailing hard-learned lessons on drawing agent boundaries, optimizing tool schemas, and managing costs while avoiding monolithic agent pitfalls. By
infoqArticles.author: Pratik Rasam

infoqArticles.title: Technological Sovereignty Requires Choice, Skills, and Support, Panelists Say During OSS EU
infoqArticles.description: European organisations can enhance their technological sovereignty by developing credible alternatives and acquiring necessary skills, rather than completely avoiding global providers. A panel discussion at the OSS EU highlighted the importance of understanding dependencies in cloud and hardware, and emphasized the need for practical choices in software for effective operational sovereignty. By Ol
infoqArticles.author: Olimpiu Pop

infoqArticles.title: Cloudflare Open Sources Decision Models for AI Agents
infoqArticles.description: During its recent “Birthday Week”, Cloudflare announced Clef, a set of open-weight AI models designed to choose between predefined options rather than generate text. Cloudflare released 9B- and 27B-parameter models, along with a platform for adapting them to specific decision-making tasks. By Renato Losio
infoqArticles.author: Renato Losio

infoqArticles.title: Survey Finds AI-Generated Code Increases Debugging and Failure Rates and Creates a Comprehension Gap
infoqArticles.description: A survey conducted by independent research firm Coleman Parkes on behalf of Undo, a company focused on scaling AI-powered root-cause analysis, found that while AI coding agents have accelerated code generation, they have shifted the primary bottleneck to debugging, code comprehension, and maintenance. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: The Async Multiprocessing Has Sound Foundations in Linux, But Further Testing Is Needed
infoqArticles.description: At Embedded Linux Conference Europe 2026, Wolfram Sang discussed the Linux building blocks for asymmetric multiprocessing (AMP). He highlighted the solid foundation but noted challenges like limited contributor coverage and fragmented testing. Sang's work on a hardware-spinlock driver revealed maintenance complexities and the need for more reviewers and testers to support evolving AMP systems. By
infoqArticles.author: Olimpiu Pop

infoqArticles.title: Grab Redesigns Counter Service Storage for 50% Lower P99 Latency
infoqArticles.description: Grab migrated its high-volume Counter Service from a wide column database to Aerospike using storage abstraction, shadow traffic, data parity validation, and gradual traffic migration. The redesigned data model consolidated time buckets into map-based records. Grab reports about 50% lower production p99 read latency, 1 TB versus 3 TB of disk usage, and 45% to 50% lower cost per node. By Leela Kumi
infoqArticles.author: Leela Kumili

infoqArticles.title: AI in Production: What Breaks, What Works, and Who Approves It? | InfoQ Webinar
infoqArticles.description: On October 14, InfoQ hosts a free 60-minute panel with five practitioners on running AI in production. They'll discuss agent autonomy and human approval, how to verify AI-generated changes, sensitive-data exposure, and production RAG. Registrants can submit questions and will receive the recording. By Artenisa Chatziou
infoqArticles.author: Artenisa Chatziou

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: The Reinvention of the Dev Team
infoqArticles.description: Hannah Foxwell shares how the surge of agentic coding forces engineering leaders to rethink team dynamics. She discusses three key anchors for navigating AI-driven velocity: building software worth building, prioritizing automated safety over speed, and preserving the human element through generalist "broken comb" skillsets and sustainable on-call practices. By Hannah Foxwell
infoqArticles.author: Hannah Foxwell

infoqArticles.title: Article: Building a Session-Ordered Kafka Pipeline in Go
infoqArticles.description: The article describes a custom implementation that provides a session-level ordering on top of Apache Kafka partitions, supporting strict message ordering across 1000s of independent channels. The solution required application-level routing, consistent hashing, retries, and contiguous watermark commits. Engineers conducted operational hardening supported by extensive performance testing. By Joshua
infoqArticles.author: Joshua Oluikpe

infoqArticles.title: Cloudflare Uses an AI Harness to Probe and Harden Its WAF
infoqArticles.description: Cloudflare placed frontier AI models inside a controlled testing harness to probe its Web Application Firewall (WAF), using blocked attacks as starting points for models to generate and refine new variations. By Matt Foster
infoqArticles.author: Matt Foster

infoqArticles.title: Spanner Omni Reaches GA, Replacing Google's Atomic Clocks and File System with Software
infoqArticles.description: Google has made Spanner Omni generally available, running its distributed SQL database on-premises, across clouds or on a laptop. Doing so meant replacing Colossus with a Colossus-like abstraction layer and TrueTime with software-based time synchronization. There is no availability SLA, and practitioners are pricing the move in tail latency and operational toil. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
infoqArticles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.title: OpenTelemetry Makes Kubernetes Attributes Processor Stable as Observability Schema Matures
infoqArticles.description: OpenTelemetry has promoted its Kubernetes Attributes Processor to v1.0.0, marking a significant step in making Kubernetes telemetry more predictable and stable across observability pipelines. By Craig Risi
infoqArticles.author: Craig Risi

infoqArticles.title: QCon London 2027 Announces 15 Tracks on Production AI, Architecture, and Engineering at Scale
infoqArticles.description: A preview of the 15-track QCon London 2027 program, covering agent evaluation and guardrails, AI-era architecture, distributed-system debugging, modern data platforms, high-performance engineering, and Staff+ leadership. By Artenisa Chatziou
infoqArticles.author: Artenisa Chatziou

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Building Resilient Platforms: Insights from 20+ Years in Mission-Critical Infrastructure
infoqArticles.description: Matthew Liste explains the 12 core principles of building scalable, reliable platforms for enterprise tech teams. From avoiding technical debt and managing deprecation to building a strong engineering culture, Liste discusses how to design infrastructure platforms that reduce complexity, streamline developer workflows, and deliver long-term value for senior architects and engineering leaders. By M
infoqArticles.author: Matthew Liste

infoqArticles.title: Flagged by the Machine: How Google Ads Suspended an Open-Source macOS Term as Malicious
infoqArticles.description: Przemyslaw Alexander Kaminski created RACE, a Rust terminal multiplexer on an infinite canvas that detaches child shells into background processes. When he launched an ad campaign, automated scanners suspended his account for malware despite clean notarization and Safe Browsing checks. The flag illustrates operational deadlocks when ad heuristics evaluate POSIX process architectures. By Olimpiu Po
infoqArticles.author: Olimpiu Pop
